movie.title: The Lost Generation
movie.overview: Set against the backdrop of the Milburn Review, teenagers in South Wales share their experience of living in 2026 and the barriers they face. The documentary explores themes of digital safety, community, role models and lack of opportunities.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Set against the backdrop of the Milburn Review, this documentary explores the struggles, barriers, and hopes of teenagers growing up in 2026 South Wales.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Set against the backdrop of the Milburn Review, 'The Lost Generation' gives voice to teenagers in South Wales navigating life in 2026. The documentary examines critical issues impacting youth today, including digital safety, community support, and a lack of role models and local opportunities. Through personal accounts, it paints an intimate yet urgent portrait of a generation fighting to build a future amidst systemic barriers.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Set in 2026, 'The Lost Generation' is a poignant documentary that examines the contemporary realities facing young people in South Wales against the backdrop of the landmark Milburn Review. Through candid interviews and personal stories, local teenagers share their first-hand experiences of growing up in an era marked by economic uncertainty and shifting social structures. The film delves deeply into the pressing issue of digital safety, highlighting the unique online challenges and mental health pressures faced by today's youth. It also investigates the erosion of local community support systems and the widespread scarcity of positive role models in these post-industrial areas. Furthermore, the documentary highlights the severe lack of educational and employment opportunities that leave many feeling trapped and disenfranchised. By interweaving these personal narratives with broader policy contexts, the narrative underscores the human impact of structural inequality. Ultimately, 'The Lost Generation' serves as both an intimate character study and a powerful call to action, amplifying voices that are too often overlooked in national conversations.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: 'The Lost Generation' provides a compelling, spoiler-free look into the lives of teenagers living in South Wales in 2026. Framing its narrative around the findings and implications of the Milburn Review, the documentary delves into the multifaceted barriers that hinder young people's social mobility and personal well-being. From navigating the complexities of digital safety and social media to coping with dwindling community resources and a shortage of accessible role models, the film illuminates the daily struggles of a generation at a crossroads. By contrasting their lived experiences with broader socioeconomic trends, 'The Lost Generation' exposes the critical gap in opportunities available to youth while honoring their resilience, perspective, and aspirations for a better future.

story_structure.climax: The documentary brings the full weight of community neglect and structural hardship into sharp focus as the teenagers confront the deep divide between policy promises and their lived experiences.
story_structure.conflict: The youth articulate the harsh realities they face, contrasting their personal aspirations against systemic barriers, lack of local opportunities, and emerging risks around digital safety.
story_structure.resolution: Synthesizes their individual stories into a poignant collective reflection, emphasizing the resilience of South Wales' youth while issuing a strong call for genuine systemic change.
story_structure.introduction: Establishes the backdrop of 2026 South Wales and introduces local teenagers navigating their daily lives amidst systemic socio-economic changes highlighted by the Milburn Review.
story_structure.risingAction: Personal testimonies reveal a growing sense of isolation, a scarcity of positive role models, and the gradual breakdown of traditional community support structures.
